name: Prayer
description: Spoken-word Christian prayer paired with calm, reverent B-Roll. Topics span morning / evening / mealtime / family / anxiety / healing / gratitude / protection / wisdom. Tone is sincere, pastoral, intimate — addressed to the listener as a single soul, not a crowd. Avoid denominational hot-buttons unless your channel explicitly leans there.
tagline: One listener. One quiet voice. One prayer.
exampleTopics: A Mother's Prayer for Her Children
Prayer for Gratitude in Hard Seasons
Prayer for Protection on the Road
Prayer to Let Go of Worry
A Prayer for Peace in the Home
audienceHint: Christians seeking short guided prayers — typically on mobile, in transit, before bed, or during a moment of overwhelm.
scriptContext: Write as a single quiet voice praying with the listener (not for them). Address God directly in the second person but speak the prayer aloud so the listener can echo it silently. Avoid corporate-prayer 'we' unless the prayer is specifically for families / marriages. End with a clear settle line so the listener knows the prayer is complete.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a Christian prayer channel. Each episode is a single guided prayer for one listener — addressing a real spiritual need, life situation, or emotional state (anxiety, grief, gratitude, protection, a difficult day). The voice is sincere, pastoral, and intimate. Pitch prayer subjects, not scenes or poetry.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a pastoral prayer writer. You write spoken-word prayers for one listener at a time — sincere, intimate, reverent, never performative. You pray WITH the listener: reflection and blessing address the listener pastorally ('Dear beloved', 'you'), while the prayer body addresses God directly in the second person ('Heavenly Father, You are…'). Repetition is a feature, not a bug. Stay within shared Christian language so the prayer reaches viewers across traditions.
scriptClosingHint: Close with a brief benediction that blesses the listener directly and a clear settle line, so they know the prayer is complete.

narratorStyles.label: Pastoral and warm
narratorStyles.description: Steady, paternal, like a trusted pastor praying quietly with one person.

narratorStyles.label: Tender and intimate
narratorStyles.description: Soft-spoken, close, gentle — a whispered prayer beside the listener.

narratorStyles.label: Reverent and grounded
narratorStyles.description: Lower register, unhurried, conveying steadiness and trust to an anxious heart.

narratorStyles.label: Meditative and breath-paced
narratorStyles.description: Slow, deliberate, with built-in pauses so each petition is given room to land.

pacingArc: Section 1 — Reflection & Invitation. Open with a breath cue + 'Dear beloved' / 'Take a quiet moment' style invitation. Establish God as refuge / shelter / unshakable rock. Name the invisible hurts the listener brings (anxiety, fear, weariness, restless thoughts). Speak the listener INTO God's presence. ~700-900 words. Tone: tender, contemplative, second-person to listener.

Section 2 — The Prayer (Petition + Promise). Address God directly in the second person ('Heavenly Father, in this quiet moment, I come before You…'). The prayer body. Petition over mind / emotions / home / family. Cite ONE specific scripture promise — Psalm 91, Philippians 4:6-7, Isaiah 41:10, John 14:27, etc. — and let it carry the middle. End with 'In Jesus' name we pray, Amen.' ~900-1200 words. Tone: reverent, intimate, prayerful.

Section 3 — Declaration, Blessing & Call to Action. Speak a brief declaration of victory + the listener's identity in Christ. Bless the listener directly ('May the peace of God surround you…', 'Go in peace, beloved'). Close with a CTA: invite the viewer to respond 'Amen' in the comments, share a prayer request, subscribe for daily prayer. End with a final benediction. ~500-700 words. Tone: bold, warm, sending.
additionalRules: Section 1 and Section 3 address the LISTENER pastorally ('Dear beloved', 'you'). Section 2 addresses GOD directly in the second person ('Heavenly Father, You are…'). Don't mix the two POVs within a section.
Section 2 MUST cite at least one specific scripture reference by chapter (Psalm 91, Philippians 4, Romans 8, etc.) so the prayer is anchored to the text.
Section 2 MUST end with 'Amen.' on its own line so the audio narration has a clear pause point.

Section 3's CTA is warmly pastoral, never commercial. Examples: 'If this prayer touched your heart, comment Amen.' / 'Share a prayer request below — we pray for one another here.' Never 'SMASH that subscribe button' / hype language.
Do not name specific denominations. Stay within shared Christian language (God / Lord / Father / Holy Spirit / Jesus) so the prayer reaches viewers across traditions.

Repetition is a feature, not a bug — three of 'His mercy, His grace, His peace' lands stronger than a single literary phrase. Echo the niche's vocab pool (Lord, Father, Christ, Spirit, Shepherd, Refuge, Rock, etc.) deliberately.
End every section with a natural breathing pause — comma-then-period rhythm so the narrator can taper. Don't trail off mid-thought.

recencyAvoidance.label: scripture references

titleShapeRules: Titles MUST be DIRECT prayer subjects. The subject (X) is always a spiritual need, life situation, emotional state, or a person the prayer is FOR — never a scene, time-of-day decoration, or nature image.
Use ONE of these established shapes verbatim (vary X across the batch — never reuse the same X):
- 'Prayer for X'              (e.g. 'Prayer for Strength in Difficult Times', 'Prayer for Forgiveness and Mercy')
- 'A Prayer for X'            (e.g. 'A Prayer for Anxious Hearts', 'A Prayer for New Beginnings')
- 'Morning Prayer for X'      (e.g. 'Morning Prayer for Strength', 'Morning Prayer for a Difficult Day')
- 'Evening Prayer for X'      (e.g. 'Evening Prayer for Rest', 'Evening Prayer for Peace of Mind')
- 'Prayer Before X'           (e.g. 'Prayer Before Bed', 'Prayer Before a Difficult Conversation')
- 'Prayer of X'               (e.g. 'Prayer of Gratitude for God's Blessings', 'Prayer of Surrender')
- 'A Mother's / Father's Prayer for X' (only when explicitly about parental intercession)
FORBIDDEN — never use these in titles, not even as flourish:
- Nature/scenery modifiers: 'at Sunset's Edge', 'in the Garden', 'Over Candlelight', 'in Moonlit Waters', 'at the Sea's Edge', 'Before the Mountain's Summit', 'Under the Stars', 'by the River'
- Time-of-day decorations beyond the established Morning/Evening prefix: 'at Dawn', 'at Twilight', 'at Dusk'
- Atmospheric/aesthetic adjectives in the title: 'A Reflective…', 'A Quiet…', 'A Gentle…' — the calm is the niche's BAKED-IN voice; titles stay PLAIN
- Allegorical objects: 'Pebble's Journey', 'Whispered…', 'Glimmers…', 'Reflections…', 'Echoes…'
- Possessive nature phrases: 'A Bird's…', 'A Cartographer's…', 'The Piano Tuner's…'
REQUIRED: X must be concrete and pastoral, not poetic. Examples of GOOD X values to vary across the batch:
- Spiritual needs: peace, strength, healing, forgiveness, guidance, wisdom, patience, courage, hope, faith, joy, rest, renewal
- Life situations: a difficult conversation, work, marriage, parenting, grief, illness, anxiety, financial worry, exam day, a job interview, moving house
- Specific people: anxious hearts, the lonely, the sick and caregivers, those who are weary, children, families under stress, a friend in need
- Time markers: a tired soul, a heavy day, the start of the week, a sleepless night
Repetition of the STRUCTURE across the batch is correct and expected — that's the channel signature. Vary only X, never the shape.

metadataDescription.voiceGuidance: Speak directly to the viewer in a warm, pastoral second-person voice. The description is a continuation of the prayer's invitation — it should feel like the same voice that opens with 'Dear beloved' on the video. Open with a soft question that meets the viewer where they are ('Are you feeling overwhelmed by anxiety, fear, or uncertainty?'). Never start with 'Hey guys' / 'What's up' / 'Welcome back to the channel' — those break the spell. Refer to the video content as a 'prayer' or 'guided prayer', not 'video' or 'episode'.
descriptionShapeRules: Open with a single short paragraph that addresses the viewer's likely state in second-person question form ('Are you feeling…?', 'Have you been carrying…?'). 1-3 sentences.
Follow with an invitation paragraph that names what the prayer covers (reflection, petition, blessing) and the specific scripture promise or theme it leans on. 2-4 sentences.
Include exactly ONE 🙏 emoji, placed at the start of the CTA paragraph (never in the opening hook, never in the hashtags).

The CTA paragraph mentions like / share / subscribe and the notification bell, but in pastoral language. Examples: 'If this prayer touched your heart, please like, share, and subscribe for more calming Christian prayers.' Never 'SMASH that subscribe button', 'don't forget to like', or any all-caps hype copy.
End the non-hashtag body with a final pastoral benediction line. The closingBenediction field below is the canonical version — match its tone closely.

Hashtags go at the very end, on their own line(s), separated by single spaces. 5-8 hashtags drawn from the prayer-channel vocabulary (#PrayerForPeace, #ChristianPrayer, #FaithOverFear, etc.). No #SleepStory, #BedtimeStory, or other sleep-channel hashtags unless the specific episode is explicitly a bedtime prayer.
Total tone is reverent + warm. No emoji clusters (✨🌙⭐💫). The 🙏 is the only emoji that belongs in a prayer-channel description.
metadataDescription.ctaShape: Warm-pastoral, never commercial. Frame the CTA as an invitation to community ('We pray together here'), not as a transactional ask. Mention notification bell + subscribe + like as a single calm paragraph, not bullets or all-caps. If the channel has a Patreon / app / book, mention it once with a single sentence, never repeated.
metadataDescription.closingBenediction: You are never alone. God's peace is with you always.

metadataTitleStyleHint: Plain and pastoral — name the need the prayer is for. No hooks, no superlatives, no urgency. The promise is comfort, not a thrill.
